items.title: call: --query, --body-field and --form-field names get a capital first letter, and --body is sent without Content-Type
items.body:
**Version:** agentsecrets 3.3.5 (linux/amd64), keychain-auth 3.3.0 in user mode.

`agentsecrets call` changes the name of every `--query`, `--body-field` and `--form-field` injection: the first letter becomes a capital. APIs with lowercase field names then ignore the injected value. A second, related gap: a plain `--body` goes out with no `Content-Type` header, so JSON APIs cannot read it.

## 1. Injection names are capitalised

**Steps:** inject a Slack channel ID into a JSON body.

    agentsecrets call --method POST \
      --url https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
      --bearer SLACK_BOT_TOKEN \
      --body '{"text":"test"}' \
      --body-field channel=SLACK_CHANNEL_ID

**Expected:** the request body is `{"channel":"<id>","text":"test"}`.

**Actual:** Slack answers `missing required field: channel`. The same happens with `--query channel=SLACK_CHANNEL_ID` on `conversations.info` (`invalid_arguments`). The same channel ID works when it is put in the URL query string directly.

**Cause:** `call` sends each injection to the proxy as a header whose name carries the target, for example `X-AS-Inject-Body-channel` ([client.go L231-L238](https://github.com/The-17/agentsecrets/blob/v3.3.5/pkg/proxy/client.go#L231-L238)). Go canonicalises header names on both sides, so the proxy receives `X-As-Inject-Body-Channel`. `parseInjections` then takes the target from the header name, which gives `Channel` ([server.go L366-L382](https://github.com/The-17/agentsecrets/blob/v3.3.5/pkg/proxy/server.go#L366-L382)).

The same design also breaks body paths that contain a dash, because the client turns `.` into `-` and the server turns every `-` back into `.`.

**Suggested fix:** carry the target in the header value instead of the header name, for example a repeatable `X-AS-Inject-Body: channel=SLACK_CHANNEL_ID`. Values are not canonicalised.

`--bearer`, `--basic` and `--header` are not affected: their target does not depend on case.

## 2. `--body` has no Content-Type, and there is no way to set one

**Steps:**

    agentsecrets call --method POST \
      --url https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
      --bearer SLACK_BOT_TOKEN \
      --body '{"channel":"C0123456789","text":"test"}'

**Expected:** the request is sent as `Content-Type: application/json`. The flag help says "Request body (JSON string)".

**Actual:** no `Content-Type` is sent, and Slack answers `missing_post_type`. A Content-Type default is only set when a `--body-field` or `--form-field` injection runs. `--header` only accepts secret key names, and `call` never fills `CallRequest.Headers` ([call.go L139-L145](https://github.com/The-17/agentsecrets/blob/v3.3.5/cmd/agentsecrets/commands/call.go#L139-L145)), so a plain header like `Content-Type` cannot be sent at all.

**Suggested fix:** default to `Content-Type: application/json` when `--body` is valid JSON, and add a flag for plain, non-secret headers (for example `--set-header Content-Type=application/json`).

## Impact

Together these block any JSON API that needs a lowercase field name in the body, Slack's `chat.postMessage` being one example. The only ways around them today are to move arguments into the URL query string, which fails above about 8 KB (HTTP 414), or to store a non-secret value such as a Content-Type as a secret.

items.title: Cursor on Windows: documented MCP setup does not work (native serve cannot find project; bridge cannot authenticate)
items.body:
## Summary

Following the documented Cursor setup on Windows does not result in a working project-scoped MCP server. Both documented routes fail:

1. `agentsecrets mcp install` writes a native `mcp serve` entry that cannot resolve the project under Cursor.
2. The bridge config shown in the docs (`npx -y @the-17/agentsecrets-mcp`) cannot authenticate: OAuth is not available on the SaaS, and the documented token-file fallback needs `agentsecrets mcp bridge auth.export`, which is not in the shipped CLI.

The CLI itself works correctly in the same repo (`doctor` healthy, `status` OK, `agentsecrets env -- ...` injection works).

## Environment

- AgentSecrets CLI 3.3.4 (current `latest` on npm)
- `@the-17/agentsecrets-mcp` 1.0.0
- Windows 11 (10.0.26300), Node >= 20
- Cursor (global `~/.cursor/mcp.json`), default SaaS server (`https://api.agentsecrets.tech/api`)
- Repo bound with `.agentsecrets/project.json` (storage mode 2, development environment), 9 secrets synced

## 1. Native `mcp serve` (what `agentsecrets mcp install` writes)

Installer output for Cursor: `{"command": "<...>/agentsecrets.exe_3.3.4", "args": ["mcp", "serve"]}`.

Steps:
1. Run `agentsecrets mcp install` from the bound repo, restart Cursor.
2. Call MCP `list_keys` / `check_key` for an existing key.

Observed:
- `list_keys` returns `no project configured in current directory`.
- `check_key` returns `exists: false` for every environment (the key exists; `agentsecrets list-secrets` in the repo shows it).
- `get_status` shows authenticated and an active session but `project: {}`.
- The running `mcp serve` process has its working directory set to the user profile folder, not the repo. The same CLI call from the user profile folder gives the same `no project configured in current directory` error.

The same result occurs when the identical entry is also placed in the repo's `.cursor/mcp.json`: Cursor still starts the server from the user profile folder. `mcp serve` accepts no flags, so there is no way to tell it which project to use. A `cwd` field in `mcp.json` is ignored by Cursor.

Expected: the docs state project context "resolves per call from the directory, explicit names, or pinned defaults". Under Cursor this does not happen for the native server.

## 2. Bridge config from the docs

The AI assistants guide (https://docs.agentsecrets.tech/integrations/ai-assistants) shows `npx -y @the-17/agentsecrets-mcp` as the config, and the installer writes something different (see above).

Steps:
1. Use the bridge config, restart Cursor.
2. Call `auth_status`: mode `cloud`, `binary: null`, no login. Next step reported: `auth_login`.
3. Call `auth_login`.

Observed: `OAuth is not available on https://api.agentsecrets.tech/api yet (no oauth endpoints)`, and the fallback instructions:

```
agentsecrets login
agentsecrets mcp bridge auth.export > ~/.agentsecrets/mcp-token
# then set AGENTSECRETS_TOKEN_FILE
```

`agentsecrets mcp --help` on CLI 3.3.4 lists only `install` and `serve`. `agentsecrets mcp bridge ...` prints the `mcp` help text, so `bridge` / `auth.export` do not exist in the shipped CLI. `secrets_list`, `project_list` and `auth_status` all fail with `No project context ... needs a control-plane login (auth_login)`, including when `project` and `path` are passed explicitly.

The MCP Bridge page (https://docs.agentsecrets.tech/integrations/mcp-bridge) describes local mode delegating to `agentsecrets mcp bridge`, which is not present in the released CLI.

## Expected

A documented path that works end to end for Cursor, for example:

- the installer writes the entry the docs describe, and the CLI release includes `mcp bridge` (local mode), or
- OAuth is live on the SaaS so `auth_login` completes, or
- the native `mcp serve` can be pointed at a project (flag or env var), or the docs state this limitation and give the supported Cursor configuration.

## Notes

No secret values are included in this report. Happy to provide more detail or test a build.

items.title: Latest version: keychain-auth error
items.body:
Saw that there was an update available and after updating the binary via homebrew, the whole thing stopped working as expected, where every command is giving me a:

`Error: keychain-auth rejected this binary path. Ensure AgentSecrets is installed in the expected location`

When investigating what came with [this release](https://github.com/The-17/agentsecrets/releases/tag/v1.1.3), I was somewhat surprised to see that it shipped with new features. Am I correct to assume that this project is not following [SemVer](https://semver.org/)?

Was expecting my upgrade to only provide fixes.

# Adhoc Mitigation 

Downgraded to 1.1.2 which worked without issues.

# Recommendations for future releases:
 
* start following semantic versioning
* add notes on breaking changes to releases (and clear migration paths)
* have such errors be more informative on what user is supposed to do when they're on upgrade path where they have installed the application via official means.
